# KitchenSink4PPT

> Everything plus the kitchen sink for Microsoft PowerPoint: the KitchenSink-family .pptx MCP server. 142 tools organized as capability packs with tiered loading from day one. Headline capability: native tweakable graphics, meaning SVG converted to grouped native PowerPoint shapes with glued connectors, editable afterward by shape identity (move the node, the arrows follow). Also the first file-based structural table operations in any PowerPoint MCP server (merge cells, insert/delete rows and columns), slide CRUD done right (insert, deep duplicate, delete with cleanup, reorder, hide), create-from-template with theme-color-referenced fills, and render-to-verify export. Engineered not to corrupt: atomic validated saves, automatic backups before every mutation, byte-identical passthrough of untouched parts, published adversarial test evidence.

Release: v1.3.1
Platform: file-based tools (the large majority) are cross-platform and need no PowerPoint installation; the export and validation tools (PDF, per-slide PNG, opens-clean check) use a local Microsoft PowerPoint via COM on Windows when present.
MCP transport: stdio.

## Install

- pip: `pip install kitchensink4ppt`
- uvx (no install): `uvx kitchensink4ppt`
- Claude Desktop: download the `.mcpb` bundle from the latest GitHub release and open it. Requires `uv` on PATH.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add ppt -s user -- kitchensink4ppt`
- Any other MCP client: run the `kitchensink4ppt` (or `ppt-mcp`) executable over stdio, e.g. `{"mcpServers": {"ppt": {"command": "kitchensink4ppt"}}}`
- MCP registry name: `io.github.KitchenSink4AI/kitchensink4ppt`

## Tiered loading (day one, not a roadmap item)

Sessions start in a lite core of 25 tools (about 7,200 tokens; the full surface is about 39,700). Packs are enabled mid-session with `enable_tools(["pack-name"])`; the server reports the token cost added. `enable_tools` and `disable_tools` send `tools/list_changed` when they change the visible set, but some clients keep the list from session or worker startup; set `KS4P_MODE` to a comma list, restart the app or session, then start a new worker, or in Claude Code enable packs in the main session before starting workers. The lite core contains no degraded stand-ins for pack capabilities, and any refusal for out-of-scope work names the exact pack and the exact enable_tools call that unlocks it.

Environment pins for clients without list_changed support, or for power users:
- `KS4P_MODE=lite` (default) | `KS4P_MODE=full` | `KS4P_MODE=graphics,design` (comma-separated pack list)
- `KS4P_PACK_POLICY=locked` prevents runtime pack changes (administrator setting)
- `KS4P_ALL_TOOLS` loads every pack at startup
- `KS4P_LOCK_TOOLS` freezes the resulting surface
- `KS4P_UPDATE_CHECK=off` disables the disclosed weekly version check. A version check never installs an update.

`get_server_info` is the authoritative runtime identity record. Use it for the installed product, package, version, homepage, sibling products, registered tool surface, lite count, released test count, and pack surface. Do not infer those values from remembered documentation.

## Capabilities by pack

Lite core (always on, ~20 tools):
`get_presentation_view` (anchored markdown projection of the deck: slides, shapes with ids, tables, notes), `apply_edits` (batched, every anchor validated first, one backup and one save per batch), `get_text`, `find_text`, `search_and_replace`, `insert_slide`, `delete_slide`, `duplicate_slide`, `reorder_slides`, placeholder/text setters, `get_slide_info`, `list_elements`, `copy_document`, `create_snapshot`, `manage_backups`, `diagnose`, `get_workflows`, `enable_tools`

graphics (the centerpiece):
`svg_to_shapes` (arbitrary SVG compiled to grouped native PowerPoint shapes; transforms flattened, arcs converted to Beziers), `insert_shape` (presets plus freeform custom geometry, gradients, theme-color fills), `insert_connector` (straight/elbow/curved, GLUED to shapes so they follow when a shape moves), `set_shape` (edit-in-place by shape id: geometry, fill, line, text, dash, arrowheads), `group_shapes`/`ungroup_shapes`, `align_shapes`, `distribute_shapes`, `set_z_order`, `format_shape_text`

tables-charts (first file-based structural table ops in the ecosystem):
`create_table`, `set_cells`, `set_cells_block`, `merge_cells`, insert/delete rows AND columns, `set_column_widths`, `format_cells` (borders, shading), `apply_table_style` (verified style GUIDs), `export_table`/`import_table` (CSV/JSON); chart creation where release testing stays green

design:
`create_presentation` (from YOUR template), `list_layouts`/`list_masters`, `apply_layout`, `get_theme` (colors and fonts), theme-color-referenced fills (schemeClr tokens that follow the theme)

assembly-export:
`set_notes`/`get_notes` (speaker notes), `manage_section`, `set_footer` and slide numbers, `hide_slide`, `export_pdf` (COM), `export_slide_image` (per-slide PNG, the render-to-verify primitive), `validate` (opens-clean plus overflow report), `extract_text`

Six packs plus the lite core, all populated in v1.1: lite (25 tools, ~7.2k tokens), graphics (27, ~8.8k), tables-charts (19, ~5.4k), design (25, ~6.8k), assembly-export (28, ~7.3k), review-sweeps (13, ~3.3k), com (5, ~0.9k). Every figure counts the whole tools/list entry the client receives, not description and schema alone. assembly-export also carries slide transitions and bounded entrance animations. review-sweeps covers threaded comments, structural deck compare, and the deck-wide font/color/language/logo sweeps plus compress. com is Windows only: PowerPoint status, zombie check, and editing decks open in PowerPoint via live=auto routing. v1.1 consolidated nine packs into six; the v1.0 names transitions-animations, review, sweeps, and com-live still resolve to their new homes in enable_tools, disable_tools, and KS4P_MODE.

## Recommended workflows

Build a diagram an audience member can still adjust:
`enable_tools(["graphics"])` -> `svg_to_shapes` (the whole diagram lands as one grouped set of native shapes with glued connectors) -> `set_shape` by id for any tweak (recolor one node, re-dash one connector) -> `enable_tools(["assembly-export"])` -> `export_slide_image` to verify visually -> `validate`.

Restructure a table nobody else can touch:
`get_presentation_view` (find the table and its anchor) -> `enable_tools(["tables-charts"])` -> insert/delete columns, `merge_cells`, `format_cells` -> `set_cells_block` for the data -> `validate`.

Build a deck on the house template:
`enable_tools(["design"])` -> `create_presentation` from the template -> `apply_layout` per slide -> populate placeholders via lite core -> theme-color fills for any added shapes -> `export_pdf`.

Heavy editing with a safety net:
`copy_document` (work on a dated copy) -> `create_snapshot` -> `get_presentation_view` -> `apply_edits` (batched, anchors validated) -> `validate` -> `export_slide_image` on changed slides.

Use `refresh-an-existing-deck` when updating an established presentation rather than rebuilding it as a new deck.

## Result contracts

Every read is bounded. When a result is incomplete, the response says so and supplies the continuation needed to retrieve the next page. Treat `page`, `returned`, and any continuation field as part of the result contract. Never infer that `slide_count` items were returned merely because the presentation contains that many slides. Continue until the response says no content remains.

Paged reads lead with `page` and `returned`. Continue until the result says no content remains. `extract_text` accepts `limit` and `offset`. `check_layout` accepts `min_group_overlap_in` and `exclude_names`.

A contrast result can be informational when the background cannot be reduced to one dependable color, including pictures, gradients and PowerPoint built-in table styles. Do not turn an undetermined result into a pass or an error.

`create_presentation(slide_size=...)` accepts only the presets listed in its tool description. It refuses an unknown value and refuses `slide_size` when a template is also supplied. A presentation created without a template defaults to 16:9; request 4:3 explicitly when required. A template keeps its own slide size. `set_slide_size` changes the canvas without moving existing content and is not a conversion back to the old layout. The 16:10 preset resizes layout boxes only.

After replacing text, inspect the result for the formatting that was preserved and for `autofit_scale_reset`. That note means the previous shrink value was cleared and the new fit is unknown. Do not claim that replacement text was refitted. Use `fit_text` when the text must be fitted deliberately.

`format_text` accepts `anchor` and `wrap`. Inside `apply_edits`, the vertical-anchor key is `text_anchor`. Unknown keys in line and fill specifications are refused by name; use only the keys listed in the tool descriptions.

`validate` may return `failed_slide_index`, `failed_slide_id`, `failed_shape_index` and `failed_shape_name`. Install `kitchensink4ppt[metrics]` for installed-font width measurement; `fit_text`, `get_autofit_state` and `check_layout` report `method="font-metrics"` or `method="estimate"`. `create_table` accepts `row_heights` and `col_widths` as a full inches list or `{index: inches}`. `KS4P_PDFTOPPM` names the poppler executable. `KS4P_PACK_POLICY` accepts only `auto` or `locked`. A complete `row_heights` or `col_widths` list resizes the table frame and the result reports `box_resized`. `validate` also reports `walk_truncated` on very large decks.

## Safety model

- Atomic validated saves; a failed operation leaves the original byte-identical.
- Automatic timestamped backup before every file mutation.
- Byte-identical passthrough of anything not being edited: animations, media, embedded objects, and unrecognized parts pass through untouched.
- Ambiguous targets are REFUSED with a candidate list; no tool ever acts on a first match.
- Slide order is resolved through the presentation's slide list, never ZIP entry order.
- Presentation writes are serialized across processes. A live lock is not reclaimed merely because it is more than ten minutes old, and a lock written by another host is not reclaimed locally. Wait for the lock or report the refusal.
- A timeout may end only a PowerPoint process started by this server. It must not end a PowerPoint process that was already running when the call began.
- Saves preserve each embedded media file's existing compression. A text or structure edit must not recompress unrelated media.
- Release evidence for v1.2: 1,635 tests, over 1,500 adversarial calls through the raw MCP stdio transport, zero corruptions, verified by opening outputs in invisible PowerPoint and failing on any repair prompt.

## Documented refusals

These are contracts. Handle them; do not retry blindly. The 12 closed codes:

- `AMBIGUOUS_LOCATION` several targets matched; use the unambiguous address from the candidates in the message.
- `NOT_FOUND` re-run get_presentation_view or get_slide_info to see current slides, ids, and anchors.
- `STALE_ANCHOR` the deck changed since the view was taken; re-run get_presentation_view and resend with fresh anchors.
- `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` close the file in PowerPoint (or wait out the other process) and retry; dual-mode tools accept live='auto' to edit the open copy instead.
- `VALIDATION_FAILED` the original file was NOT modified; the message says what the produced package failed.
- `APP_NOT_RUNNING` this operation needs PowerPoint installed and reachable.
- `APP_BUSY` PowerPoint is showing a dialog or running a command; clear it and retry.
- `APP_BLOCKED` PowerPoint is not answering; wait or restart it.
- `PROTECTED_VIEW` click Enable Editing in PowerPoint first.
- `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` structurally unsupported or password-protected content, refused instead of written partially.
- `CONFLICT` the destination path exists and overwrite was not requested.
- `BAD_PARAMS` bad arguments, including a path outside the configured sandbox roots (`KS4P_ALLOWED_ROOTS`).

Refusals are the reliability feature, not the failure mode. A refusal names
what was wrong, leaves the file untouched, and carries the next call in
`hint`. Retrying the same call unchanged is never the fix.

## The KitchenSink family

- KitchenSink4Word (the original fixture, 221 operations across 110 tools for .docx): https://kitchensink4.ai/KitchenSink4Word/
- KitchenSink4XL (the electrical aisle, 69 tools for .xlsx, every value labeled calculated, cached, or absent): https://kitchensink4.ai/KitchenSink4XL/
- KitchenSink4Web (the garden section, browser automation with budget-priced page reads and a consent ladder): https://kitchensink4.ai/KitchenSink4Web/
- Family storefront: https://kitchensink4.ai/products/
